Keep the detections of some animals or species

Source: R/filter_common.R
filter_animals.Rd

Cuts a detection set to the animals of the given species, or to the given animals, as a logged step. Cut a set after detset(): detset() gives a reused transmitter's detections to the animal released last before each one, and it can do so only when every animal is in the animals table. A cut to one species made before detset() can give the detections of another species' animal to an animal of that species. Run audit_listening() and check_detset() before the cut too: both read every transmitter the receivers logged, and a receiver that heard only other species would look silent after it.

Usage

filter_animals(x, species = NULL, animals = NULL, transmitters = NULL)

Arguments

x

A detset().

species

Optional species to keep, matched to species in the animals table, ignoring case.

animals

Optional animal_id values to keep. With species too, an animal is kept when it meets either.

transmitters

Optional transmitter codes kept whatever their animal, such as the reference tags.

Value

x with the detections kept, the animals table cut to the animals kept, and one log record (reasons other_animal and no_animal).

Details

The animals table is cut to the animals kept. Detections with no animal_id, such as reference tags, are removed unless their transmitter is in transmitters.

See also

Other filters: filter_deployment_period(), filter_duplicates(), filter_min_detections(), filter_min_lag(), filter_post_release(), filter_release(), filter_speed(), filter_tag_life(), minimum_lags()

Examples

study <- detqc_example
dets <- detset(study$detections, study$deployments, study$animals)
st02_only <- filter_animals(dets, animals = "ST-02")
writeLines(strwrap(detset_log(st02_only)$reason[2], width = 72))
#> removed 2,024 of 3,297 detections (61.39%); 3 animals lost every
#> detection
